summary.text: Charles Hoelter, a San Mateo-based Republican and retired UPS supervisor, lost the November 3, 2026 election for California's 15th Congressional District to Kevin Mullin.
His campaign site describes him as a conservative advocate for "freedom, faith, and family."

paragraphs.text: Hoelter graduated from Lincoln High School and earned a bachelor's degree from San Francisco State University in 1989.
He describes himself as a retired UPS supervisor who worked at the company for more than 25 years.
He says he lived in San Francisco for 27 years before moving to San Mateo County, where he has lived for 36 years, and that he has been married for 31 years and has three children.
According to his campaign website, Hoelter has spent years building relationships in the community and listening to working families, small business owners, veterans and law enforcement.
He advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary in second place with 18.4% of the vote (30,476 votes), and his Ballotpedia survey response lists the San Mateo Republican Party as an endorser.
He described his campaign priorities as including term limits, voter ID and apprenticeship programs in high schools.
He received 21.4% of the vote to Kevin Mullin's 78.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
